# PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Vejle)

PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Vejle) is a local psychiatric unit in Vejle, Denmark, that appears in the Danish ADHD-databasen's 2024 quality report as one of the treatment units assessed against national ADHD care indicators. The unit's performance is documented for two separate indicators, with sharply contrasting results.

On Indicator 10 — which measures the share of adult treatment courses in which the patient's need for social support was assessed no later than 120 days after treatment start — PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Vejle) achieved only 47 % (confidence interval 36–58), based on 40 out of 86 eligible courses, and was marked "Nej" (No) against the compliance flag[^src1]. This falls well short of the national development goal of 90 % completion for this indicator[^src1]. The unit's result sits within a wider national picture in which Indicator 10 was reported for the first time in this cycle, showing substantial shortfalls both nationally (37 %) and across regions (14–52 %), prompting the steering group behind the ADHD database to discuss underlying causes — including registration practices and data quality from child/adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinics and private hospitals — and to commit to improving registration practices going forward.

By contrast, on a separate indicator reported later in the same document (pages 56–60), PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Vejle) scored 91 % (confidence interval 82–96), based on 78 out of 86 courses[^src2]. This section of the report concerns Indicator 11, which measures the proportion of adult ADHD patients in medication treatment within 120 days of starting a treatment pathway — the first time this indicator has been calculated for adults, following the 2024 expansion of the ADHD database to include adult patients. National results for Indicator 11 showed considerable regional variation, ranging from 85 % in Region Nordjylland to 37 % in Region Hovedstaden, a spread attributed mainly to differences in registration practices rather than genuine differences in clinical care.

Taken together, the two data points illustrate a unit performing far below target on assessing patients' social support needs, while performing strongly on ensuring timely medication treatment — a divergence that mirrors the broader national pattern of inconsistent registration and reporting across Danish psychiatric units in the 2024 ADHD database cycle.
